learning_objective: Recognize life-threatening symptoms requiring immediate medical attention.
key_points: Early recognition prevents maternal and newborn death; complications can arise at any stage; emergency transport and funds should be planned in advance.
do_actions: Learn and memorize signs; identify nearest facility; arrange emergency transport/funds.
seek_care_if: Vaginal bleeding; convulsions; fever; severe headache; blurred vision; severe abdominal pain; respiratory distress.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; SMNH Roadmap 2030

learning_objective: Understand dietary requirements for a healthy pregnancy.
key_points: Healthy eating prevents excessive weight gain; undernourished women need extra energy and protein; diet influences birth weight and maternal health.
do_actions: Eat one extra meal per day; eat healthy and diverse food; stay active throughout pregnancy.
avoid: High-protein supplements (unless undernourished); routine Vitamin B6, C, E, or D supplements.
seek_care_if: Excessive weight gain; lack of weight gain.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; Who Guidelines ANC; NDHS2022

learning_objective: Understand the importance of daily iron and folic acid supplementation.
key_points: IFA prevents maternal anaemia, sepsis, and low birth weight; supplementation should continue for 180 days during pregnancy.
do_actions: Take IFA tablets daily as prescribed; store tablets in a dry place; continue for 45 days postpartum.
seek_care_if: Extreme pallor (paleness); feeling too weak to stand.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; Who Guidelines ANC

learning_objective: Monitor the baby’s activity to ensure well-being.
key_points: Maternal perception of fetal movement is a key assessment tool; reduced movement is associated with fetal distress or hypoxia.
do_actions: Be aware of the baby's movements daily; report changes immediately.
avoid: Routine daily kick charts (only recommended for research context).
seek_care_if: Fetal movements stop or significantly decrease.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; WHO recommendations on maternal health

learning_objective: Prepare all necessary items and plans for a safe childbirth.
key_points: Facility delivery with a skilled birth attendant is safer than home; a birth plan reduces delays in receiving emergency care.
do_actions: Identify facility; choose a birth companion; arrange transport; save money; identify blood donors; prepare MNCH card.
seek_care_if: Signs of labour (contractions, leaking fluid, "water broke").
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; SMNH Roadmap 2030

learning_objective: Prepare for immediate and exclusive breastfeeding after birth.
key_points: Initiation should occur within one hour of birth; exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for the first 6 months.
do_actions: Practice skin-to-skin contact; use responsive feeding; exclusive breastfeeding only.
avoid: Pre-lacteal feeds (sugar water, honey, etc.); use of bottles or teats.
seek_care_if: Baby not feeding well; sore nipples; breast engorgement.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; WHO recommendations on maternal health

learning_objective: Understand options for spacing future pregnancies for health.
key_points: Postpartum family planning (PPFP) prevents short birth intervals; intervals <24 months increase mortality risk for mother and baby.
do_actions: Discuss options with provider; initiate a method before facility discharge if desired.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; SMNH Roadmap 2030; NDHS2022

learning_objective: Manage common discomforts of pregnancy safely.
key_points: Hormonal and mechanical changes cause common symptoms; non-pharmacological relief is effective for many.
do_actions: Use ginger or Vitamin B6 for nausea; elevate legs for oedema; use wheat bran for constipation; do regular exercise for back pain.
seek_care_if: Symptoms persist or become severe (e.g., persistent vomiting).
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; Who Guidelines ANC

learning_objective: Understand the harmful effects of tobacco and alcohol.
key_points: Tobacco and alcohol increase risks for mother and baby; second-hand smoke exposure is dangerous.
do_actions: Quit tobacco use; avoid alcohol and other substances; lower caffeine intake (<300mg/day).
avoid: Smoking or use of smokeless tobacco.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; Who Guidelines ANC

learning_objective: Recognize and seek help for maternal depression.
key_points: Postpartum depression affects maternal well-being and child care; symptoms can be screened and treated.
do_actions: Talk to a healthcare worker about feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or lack of interest.

learning_objective: Ensure protection against tetanus for the mother and newborn.
key_points: Tetanus toxoid-containing vaccine (TTCV) prevents neonatal mortality; multiple doses are required based on history.
do_actions: Receive the scheduled TTCV injection; check and update vaccination history.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; WHO recommendations on maternal health

learning_objective: Understand specific risks and care needs for young mothers.
key_points: Adolescents face higher risks of complications and social barriers to care; facility delivery is recommended.
do_actions: Conduct HEADSS assessment; prioritize facility delivery; ensure social support.

learning_objective: Identify early symptoms of high blood pressure disorders.
key_points: Preeclampsia is a leading cause of maternal death; symptoms often appear in the second half of pregnancy.
do_actions: Monitor blood pressure and proteinuria at every visit; report severe headaches.
seek_care_if: Severe headache; blurred vision; upper epigastric (stomach) pain.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; WHO recommendations on maternal health

learning_objective: Identify support for safety and reproductive health.
key_points: IPV is a risk factor for maternal and fetal death; disclosure in a private setting is essential for support.
do_actions: Disclose safety concerns to a trusted provider; seek referral to social services.
seek_care_if: Traumatic injury; repeated intrusive partner presence.
source: Digital ANC Who guidelines; WHO recommendations on maternal health
